Parkes Weber syndrome: The patient's symptoms of an enlarged right upper limb, difficulty in function, and presence of multiple distinct swollen areas over the entire arm and shoulder girdle, along with the presence of phleboliths and dilated tortuous anechoic lesions involving the upper limb and periscapular region, could also be consistent with Parkes Weber syndrome, although the absence of arteriovenous fistulas makes it less likely.
